output.brief: The rise in Corvane's mishandled bags is most likely a tag-printing problem, not a handling problem. Since 1 September, bags carrying tags printed on the new Fennick Labels stock fail automatic reading about 11.8% of the time, against 1.5% on the old Brackwater stock. The same airport arrays read Tessaly-handled transfer and Pelion tags normally. On 14–16 October, counters that fell back to Brackwater stock from stores read at 1.6%, while kiosks using Fennick stock that same week failed at 12.1%. Those failed bags are diverted to manual encoding and then miss cart closure. I have not separated a defective batch from a printer heat-setting problem, and the handler change is not supported as the main driver. Confidence is moderate, around 55–70%. Next steps: do not issue the breach notice on the current evidence, since it would penalise Tessaly for a cause that is likely upstream. Return counters to Brackwater stock now, which is reversible and within contract until 31 December. Test the Fennick stock against the printer heat settings, using the Teyra bulletin and a controlled print trial, before filing any defect claim. Bring HBAA into the review.
